HOMAGE TO MARTYRS OF THE QUIT INDIA MOVEMENT 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, today is the 63rd Anniversary of the 
historic day when the "Quit India Movement' was launched in 1942 under 
the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi. The whole nation responded to the 
clarion call of Gandhiji and participated in the Movement with single-minded 
commitment and dedication which culminated in our achieving 
Independence five years later. 
We pay our humble and respectful homage to all those martyrs who 
gave their lives, and also to those who suffered untold sufferings for the 
cause of our freedom. 
I would request hon. Members to rise in their places and observe silence 
as a mark of respect to the memory of martyrs. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute)

Pollution of underground water 
†*221. SHRI JANARDAN DWIVEDI: 
SHRI MOTILAL VORA: 
Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government's attention has been drawn to the report of the 
School of Environmental Sciences of Jawaharlal Nehru University which 
says that underground water is getting highly polluted due to a landfill 
arising in the form of hills in the Capital and in its bordering areas; 
(b) if so, the steps being taken by Government to curb this; 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(d) the concrete arrangements being made by Government to check 
pollution of ground water and by when? 
THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI PRIYARANJAN 
DASMUNSI): (a) to (d) School of Enviro nmental Sciences, Jawaharlal Nehru 
University, New Delhi has carried out a study on ground water quality in 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
4 

[9 August, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
vicinity of Bhalsava landfill site in Delhi. As per the study, ground water 
samples contains iron, manganese, copper, lead, nickel and zinc. The 
study has also indicated that the c oncentrations of metal increase as 
approached towards landfill. 
The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) has also carried out a 
study on heavy metal levels in ground water samples surrounding the 
Bhalsava landfill site. The studies have indicted presence of iron and zinc. 
However, samples collected have  shown signs of non-traceable 
concentration in respect of lead, chromium and cadmium. 
As per Municipal Solid Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2000, 
the local bodies are required to undertake improvement of existing landfill 
sites and design new landfill sites to protect ground water contamination. 
The Municipal Corporation of Delhi is in the process for setting up of new 
landfill facilities and also are contemplating to set up waste processing 
plant so that the burden on landfill for disposal of waste could be minimized.

Improvement in air traffic infrastructure 
*224. SHRI SHAHID SIDDIQUI: Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a shortage of ATC officers at most of 
the major airports, which is making our airports unsafe; 
(b) what steps have been taken to improve the infrastructure with 63 per 
cent increase in air traffic in the last five years; and 
(c) whether it is also a fact that due to  lack of area control centres there 
are gaps in the Indian skies and if so, what steps have been taken to 
remove these gaps? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION 
(SHRI PRAFUL PATEL): (a) There is some shortage of ATC officers at 
some airports. However, there is no compromise on safety as all the ATC 
units are manned by qualified Air Traffic Controllers and ICAO Standards 
and Recommended Procedures are being followed strictly. 
(b) Steps have been taken to provide additional ground infrastructure 
such as parallel taxiways, rapid exit taxiways and parking stands to 
enhance airside capacity at major airp orts. Additional air traffic routes 
through airport capacity (EMARSSH) project and Reduced Vertical 
Separation Minima (RVSM) have also been implemented to accommodate 
more number of aircraft in a defined airspace. Automatic Dependent System/ 
Controller Pilot Data Link Communication system has been installed at 
Kolkata, Chennai, Delhi and Mumbai airports. In addition, the Air Traffic 
Control facilities are also being regularly augmented through improvement 
of Communication, Navigation & Surveillance infrastructure, on the basis 
of the requisition received from user agencies so as to meet the growing 
air traffic requirements.

(c) There are 11 Area Control Centres (ACC) which are covering major 
portion of the Indian airspace. Some of the ACCs are not continguous and 
are independent of each other due to  the gaps in Very High Frequency 
(VHF) coverage and radar coverage. The gaps in VHF coverage is being 
covered by installing Remote Controlled Air Ground Communication 
(RCAGC) systems at various locations. Additional radars and radar 
networking are also planned. Besides, in collaboration with Indian Space 
Research Organization (ISRO), AAI is implementing GPS and GEO

for providing augmentation service. A Dedicated Satellite Communication

Detection of adulterated cases 
†*227. SHRI NAND KISHORE YADAV: Will the Minister of PETROLEUM 
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the petrol and petroleum products are being 
adulterated with the nexus of the officers of the public sector undertakings; 
(b) if so, the reaction of Government thereto; and 
(c) the details of powers vested with these officers to stop adulteration 
and the number of cases of abuse of th ese powers reported during the last 
three years? 
THE MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI MANI 
SHANKAR AIYAR): (a) The Public Sector Oil Marketing Companies 
(OMCs) have reported that they have no established case of involvement 
of their officers in adulteration cases. 
(b) Does not arise in view of (a) above. However, there are Provisions 
under the Conduct Rules as also the Marketing Discipline Guidelines 
(MDG), 2005, to take action against offi cers found involved in irregularities/ 
malpractices, including adulteration. 
(c) The officers are empowered to inspect retail outlets, draw samples 
and send the samples to notified laboratories for testing. They are also 
empowered to carry out search and seizure under the provisions of various 
control orders issued under the Esse ntial Commodities Act. In case any 
irregularity/malpractice is established, action is initiated against the erring 
dealer under the MDG/Dealership Agreement. OMCs have reported that 
no case of abuse of these powers by their officers has been established 
during the last three years.
